subject: Chemistry
title: The Element on Your Ceiling: The Actinoids
summary: An ionisation smoke detector holds about 1 microcurie of americium-241, a man-made actinoid. The actinoids are the fourteen elements thorium (90) to lawrencium (103), filling 5f: [Rn] 5f¹⁻¹⁴ 6d⁰⁻¹ 7s². Because 5f, 6d and 7s are close in energy they show a wide range of oxidation states: +3 is common, but Th reaches +4, Pa +5, U +6 (as in uranyl UO₂²⁺) and Np and Pu +7, after which the maximum falls. 5f electrons shield poorly, so the actinoid contraction is larger than the lanthanoid contraction. The metals are very reactive (boiling water gives oxide and hydride; HCl attacks them; nitric acid forms a protective oxide layer; alkalies have no action). All actinoids are radioactive: Th-232 (≈ 14 billion years) and U-238 (≈ 4.5 billion years) occur in nature, while the elements beyond uranium are man-made and the last ones survive only minutes to hours.
keyPoints: **5f ≈ 6d ≈ 7s** in energy → a wide range of oxidation states.
**+3** common; first half climbs: Th +4, Pa +5, U +6, **Np, Pu +7**; later ones fall back.
**UO₂²⁺**: x − 4 = +2 → U = +6; uranyl makes uranium glass glow green under UV.
Reactive metals: boiling water → oxide + hydride; HCl attacks; HNO₃ → protective oxide layer; alkalies: no action.
**All radioactive**: Th-232 ≈ 14 billion years, U-238 ≈ 4.5 billion years; beyond U man-made (Np, 1940).
Am-241 in smoke detectors; Pu-238 heat powers Voyager and Curiosity.

blocks.p: Irregular configurations relate to the stability of f⁰, f⁷ and f¹⁴ (e.g. Cm: [Rn] 5f⁷ 6d¹ 7s²). Magnetic properties are more complex than those of the lanthanoids, and ionisation enthalpies of early actinoids are lower than those of early lanthanoids. NCERT gives the later half-lives as "a day to 3 minutes for lawrencium"; use that wording in CBSE answers.

quiz.q: The actinoids are the elements from:
quiz.explain: The actinoids are the fourteen elements from thorium (Th, Z = 90) to lawrencium (Lr, Z = 103), in which the 5f orbitals are progressively filled.

quiz.q: The general configuration of the actinoids is:
quiz.explain: General electronic configuration of the actinoids: [Rn] 5f¹⁻¹⁴ 6d⁰⁻¹ 7s².

quiz.q: Actinoids show more oxidation states than lanthanoids because:
quiz.explain: The 5f, 6d and 7s levels are of comparable energies, so actinoids show a wider range of oxidation states than lanthanoids.

quiz.q: The maximum oxidation state shown by an actinoid is:
quiz.explain: +3 is the general oxidation state of the actinoids; the maximum is +7 (Np, Pu).

quiz.q: The oxidation state of uranium in UO₂²⁺ is:
quiz.explain: Uranium shows +6 in the uranyl ion UO₂²⁺ (U = +6, since x − 4 = +2).

quiz.q: Compared with the lanthanoid contraction, the actinoid contraction from element to element is:
quiz.explain: Actinoid contraction: the size of atoms and M³⁺ ions decreases steadily across the series, and it is greater from element to element than the lanthanoid contraction because 5f electrons shield poorly.

quiz.q: Which statement is true of the actinoids?

quiz.explain: A household ionisation smoke detector contains about 1 microcurie (≈ 0.3 microgram) of americium-241, a man-made actinoid.

quiz.q: Which actinoids occur in nature in substantial amounts?
quiz.explain: Only thorium and uranium occur in nature in substantial amounts; actinium and protactinium occur as decay products; elements beyond uranium (transuranium) are essentially man-made.

quiz.q: Most actinoid metals are only slightly affected by nitric acid because:
quiz.explain: Hydrochloric acid attacks all actinoid metals, but most are only slightly affected by nitric acid because a protective oxide layer forms; alkalies have no action.

simulation.reason: The topic is configurations, oxidation states and radioactivity; the video, tables, memory cards and 25 workbook questions teach it, and there is no continuous variable a student would usefully change.
